_comment: CLAUDE.md size ratchet CEILING (W1-T503, MASTER-PLAN 8A). capBytes is the only figure declared here -- the actual byte size is measured fresh from the committed CLAUDE.md by `node scripts/claude-md-budget-ratchet.mjs` on every run (W1-T1234: a stored measured figure went stale on every edit to CLAUDE.md and reddened the gate for a reason no PR caused). capBytes carries deliberate headroom over the file's typical size, which is a change from the zero-headroom shape this baseline held until 2026-08-22 -- see bumpRationale for the current raise and priorBumpRationale for the one that retired zero-headroom. IT IS NO LONGER A ROUND BOUNDARY: 65536 (64 KiB) was chosen for legibility on 2026-08-22 and the 2026-08-28 raise traded that legibility for a stated +2000 increment, so do not 'restore' a power of two by rounding this figure in either direction. The ceiling still fails closed and still only ever ratchets UP by a reviewed bump that says why growth is right; never lower it to make a red PR pass, and never raise it to paper over an unreviewed dump of new rules.
bumpRationale: LOWERED 67536 -> 44000 by W1-T2507 on 2026-08-31, THE FIRST TIME THIS RATCHET HAS EVER MOVED DOWN. The two prior entries below raised the cap twice because the file itself kept growing and folding it further kept costing more than it saved -- W1-T2507 changed the OTHER variable: it moved content OUT of CLAUDE.md rather than compressing what stayed. Three moves, none of them a rule deletion: (1) 19 bullets that each named a concrete repo path became learnings/architecture.yaml entries whose files: glob matches exactly that path, so the fact now reaches the task that governs it and no other -- the destination this repo already built and measured (W1-T33/W1-T38). Three MORE bullets were drafted for the same move and REVERTED: existing regression tests (test/docs-claims.test.ts, test/rule-citations-match-their-rule.test.ts, test/ci-gate-reaggregate.test.ts, test/fleet-heartbeat-image-sha.test.ts) pin their exact prose inside CLAUDE.md itself, proving those particular facts are read by every task author regardless of files: -- not just editors of the one file they happen to name -- so migrating them would have LOST reach rather than preserved it; they stayed. (2) the 'Operating this host' section -- rules about the daemon's own mac-mini host (shared node_modules, launchd, the worktree-reaping directory) that a containerised worker can never act on -- moved to docs/operator-guide.md, the document its actual reader (a human operating that host) already consults; ONE bullet from that section (the mount-vs-image-rebuild boundary) came back for the same reason as above -- a worker editing deploy/ needs it, proven by test/fleet-heartbeat-image-sha.test.ts. (3) the five dated 'Lessons from <date>' sections, an append-only log the file's own maintenance rule forbids, folded into the topical sections they belong to, with letter sequences renumbered so no gap is left. The file measures 42606 bytes after all moves (vs 67535 before, one byte under the old cap), and 44000 restores deliberate headroom -- about 1400 bytes -- so the ratchet keeps its designed job of forcing a fold-or-migrate decision on the NEXT addition rather than sitting so far under cap that growth goes unnoticed for weeks. NEVER raise this back toward 67536 to make a red PR pass without first checking whether the growth is itself a bullet that names a concrete path or belongs in a dated section -- those have a cheaper move than raising the cap, PROVIDED no existing test pins that bullet's prose inside CLAUDE.md itself (grep test/*.test.ts for the bullet's distinctive phrase before moving it). See learnings/architecture.yaml's newest entries (`migrated from CLAUDE.md`, W1-T2507) and docs/operator-guide.md's new 'Operating this host' section for the migrated content itself. CORRECTION (W1-T2759): every figure here prices the INTERACTIVE lane. A dispatched worker never loads CLAUDE.md at all -- spawnWorker passes settingSources: [], which the SDK documents as isolation mode requiring 'project' to load CLAUDE.md files.
priorBumpRationale: Raised 65536 -> 67536 (+2000) by an OPERATOR DECISION on 2026-08-28. THIS IS THE THIRD CONVERSATION ABOUT THIS NUMBER, and the 2026-08-22 entry set the bar for it: 'the folds are expensive now' carried once and cannot carry twice without new evidence. THE NEW EVIDENCE IS A MEASURED RATE, NOT A FEELING. CLAUDE.md stood at 65488 bytes against the 65536 ceiling -- 48 BYTES FREE -- and a retro on 2026-08-28 harvested rules it could not land: the drafted additions measured +1374, over the cap by 1326, so the run opened NO PR and reported the ceiling as the blocker instead. That is the cost this raise buys off: a ceiling that stops a rule from being written at all is no longer taxing prose, it is dropping knowledge on the floor. THE ARITHMETIC, SAID PLAINLY SO THE NEXT READER CAN CHECK IT: growth has run about 192 bytes/day over the file's lifetime and about 374 bytes/day over the last fortnight, so +2000 buys roughly five days at the recent rate and rather less once this PR's own +1397 is spent -- 67536 - 66885 = 651 BYTES OF HEADROOM THE MOMENT THIS LANDS, under two days at the recent rate. A FOURTH RAISE IS THEREFORE FORESEEABLE AND MUST NOT BE AUTOMATIC; whoever asks for it needs evidence this one did not have. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE, unchanged from 2026-08-22: the ratchet still fails closed, still runs unconditionally in ci.yml, and still reports size against cap on every run. NEVER lower capBytes to make a red PR pass, and never raise it to paper over an unreviewed dump of new rules. (The 2026-08-22 raise's own rationale -- 62733 -> 65536, retiring the zero-headroom shape -- preceded this one and is no longer carried verbatim here; see git history at this file's prior revisions for its full text.)
